questions.q: What does a Nice Guy typically do in a conflict?
a: He avoids it and agrees just to keep the peace
He argues until the other person gives in
He asks a friend to speak for him
He demands an apology before continuing
questions.why: The overview says Nice Guys inhibit their personality and avoid conflict at all costs.

questions.q: Why is overpleasing others harmful, according to the summary?
a: It erodes boundaries and breeds frustration
It makes you too popular at work
It costs too much time and money
It makes others jealous of you
questions.why: Lesson 2 says blurry boundaries let people use you and lose respect, which builds frustration.

questions.q: What should you do when someone's opinion differs from yours?
a: Say so and stand behind your own view
Agree quickly to end the tension
Stay quiet and revisit it later
Let them decide for both of you
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to analyze a different view, but be vocal when you disagree rather than being walked over.

questions.q: What are the three wrong assumptions behind Nice Guy behavior?
a: Being nice earns love, reciprocity and a problem-free life
Conflict builds respect, honesty and closeness
Boundaries attract love, trust and stability
Speaking up creates safety, clarity and peace
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists the beliefs that niceness earns love, that needs will be returned and that avoiding upset solves life.

questions.q: What does the summary say about a relationship that ends when you reclaim respect?
a: You have lost only someone who drained you
You have lost your best chance at love
You should have compromised more first
You will struggle to trust anyone again
questions.why: Lesson 2 says if the relationship ends as you claim respect, you have lost nothing but an energy drainer.
